results.text: Thank you. [#0](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-0)

Good afternoon to our participants in Europe, and good morning to everyone joining from across the Americas welcome to Elis 2025 Half Year Results presentation. [#1](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-1)
I am Xavier Martire, CEO of Elis, speaking to you from Paris, and I'm joined by our CFO, Louis Guyot. [#2](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-2)
I will begin with a brief overview of the key highlights from the first half of the year. [#3](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-3)
Then I will hand over to Luis who will walk you through the financial results in detail. [#4](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-4)
After that, I'd return to share our main CSR achievements and provide an update on our outlook for the remainder of 2025. [#5](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-5)
We'll then open the floor for a Q&A session. [#6](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-6)
And as always, Nicolas Buron will be available after the call to address any further questions. [#7](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-7)
Before we begin, please take a moment to read the disclaimer. [#8](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-8)
For the first half of 2025 confirm Eli's ability to deliver solid results in a demanding macroeconomic context. [#10](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-10)

Revenue reached EUR 2.34 billion in the first half, up 4.3%, including 3.5% organic growth which is in line with our long-term target of 4% when adjusted for minus 0.5 points calendar impact. [#11](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-11)
Adjusted EBITDA increased by 5.1% to EUR 813.8 million with a margin expansion of plus 30 basis points to 34.7%. [#12](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-12)
Adjusted EBIT rose by plus 3% to EUR 353.8 million with a slight margin decline of 20 basis points to 15.1%. [#13](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-13)
Headline net income per share was up plus 3%, reaching on a fully diluted basis. [#14](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-14)

Free cash flow stood at EUR 31 million and the financial leverage ratio as of June 30, 2025, was down 14 basis points at 1.92x compared to June 2024. [#15](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-15)

This performance reflects the strength of our model and the momentum behind our growth drivers, including a strong commercial dynamic supported by new contract wins in the workwear segment, solid performance in Hospitality, especially in Q2, positive pricing momentum across all regions offsetting cost inflation, operational improvements and productivity gains across our operations. [#17](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-17)
Finally, it confirms all of its 2025 financial objectives, as communicated last March. [#18](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-18)
Let's now move to the Slide 6, which focuses on top line growth drivers in the first half of 2025. [#20](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-20)

With 70% of its business resilient to economic fluctuations and primarily based on fixed fee billing Elis remains firmly focused on its growth strategy. [#21](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-21)

In the first half of 2025, Elis recorded plus 4.3% top line growth illustrating once again the effectiveness of its commercial and strategic choices. [#22](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-22)

Growth was mainly driven by strong commercial momentum in workwear, supported by continued outsourcing trends across all geographies, both in [indiscernible] This quarter was further reinforced by the ramp-up of additional sales team in high potential countries. [#23](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-23)
Hospitality also performed satisfactory, especially in France, where Q2 benefited from a favorable comparable base. [#24](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-24)
Activity in Southern Europe remain dynamic, while the U.K. was more subdued. [#25](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-25)
As anticipated, the calendar effects weighed modestly on organic growth in H1, [ trimming ] about 0.5 points. [#27](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-27)
notably positive pricing dynamics across all markets helped offset the impact of inflation on our cost base. [#28](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-28)
Revenue growth was also supported by a plus 1.8% contribution from M&A largely stemming from a recent acquisition in Central Europe. [#29](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-29)
Lastly, we recorded minus 1% FX impact, mostly due to the depreciation of Latin American currencies. [#30](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-30)

Let's now turn to Slide 7, which highlights our long-term ambition to replicate the successful French model in terms of footprint, scale and breadth of services across all other revenue. [#32](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-32)
As local network density increases, we naturally extend our offering to smaller clients. [#33](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-33)
This strategy is already well underway and proving highly effective in markets like in the U.K. and Brazil. [#34](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-34)

We also continue to expand our service portfolio in countries where some of our offerings were not yet available, such as [ pest ] control and [indiscernible] both of which benefit from strong long-term hygiene trends. [#35](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-35)

A clear example of our ability to save targeted opportunities is the recent contract wins in the U.K. and Spain for resident [ client ] services, nursing homes, segments where outsourcing still hold significant untapped potential. [#36](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-36)

These multiple growth avenues go all in on with the need to scale up our sales force in countries where we see strong organic potential. [#37](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-37)

We remain committed to proactively capturing every opportunity and will, therefore, continue to invest in local sales team going forward. [#38](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-38)
Let's now take a look at each of our geographies, starting with France. [#40](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-40)
France delivered another solid performance in the first half of 2025 with revenue growth at plus 3.1%, which was entirely organic. [#41](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-41)

Growth was supported by good commercial momentum across all end markets, with a particularly strong Q2 in hospitality, thanks to a favorable comparison base. [#42](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-42)
As in previous periods, pricing adjustments helped to offset the impact of inflation of our cost base. [#43](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-43)
Importantly, the EBITDA margin continued to improve, reaching 41.8%, up plus 90 basis points year-on-year. [#44](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-44)

This margin improvement was driven by logistic savings and efficiency gains in our workshops including higher productivity and more efficient use of energy and water. [#45](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-45)

France remains a mature and well-structured geography for Elis, and we continue to focus on margin improvement through industrial excellence and disciplined commercial execution. [#46](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-46)
Moving on to Slide 9. [#47](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-47)
Let's focus on Central Europe which posted a strong home growth of plus 8.8% in the first half. [#48](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-48)

Acquisitions played a significant role, contributing plus 5.7% to regional growth, while organic growth remained solid at plus 2.6% despite the calendar headwind estimated at minus 0.6% for the region. [#49](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-49)

Growth was primarily driven by strong commercial momentum in the [indiscernible] the region continues to be highly diversified health care industry together account for 70% of the portfolio, followed by trade and services and hospitality. [#50](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-50)

In Germany, top line growth was more selective, particularly in the Public Health care segment where we maintain a cautious stance due to the ongoing budgetary constraints within the public health system. [#51](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-51)

On the profitability side, EBITDA margin improved by 100 bps to 32.3%, mainly reflecting lower general costs sustained operational progress in Germany, which alone delivered an impressive plus 240 basis points of margin expansion. [#52](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-52)
Moving on to the next slide. [#53](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-53)

Let's now take a look at Scandinavia and Eastern Europe, a region with solid fundamentals, but more challenging 1 month in the first half. [#55](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-55)
Reported revenue was up plus 2.6%, including approximately plus 2% organic growth restated from the calendar effect. [#56](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-56)

Commercial momentum was mixed across geographies we experienced volume losses in Denmark, where the competitive environment remained particularly intense by contracts, Norway, Finland and the Baltics performed well, showing positive trend. [#57](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-57)
As in other regions, pricing adjustments were more limited and due to lower inflation level in early 2025. [#58](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-58)
The negative calendar effect in Q1 weighed slightly on performance estimated at minus 0.4% for the region. [#59](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-59)
On the profitability side, the EBITDA margin declined by 50 bps to 34.4%. [#60](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-60)
While Sweden maintained a stable margin, Denmark continued to face pressure. [#61](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-61)
Encouragingly, we saw strong margin improvement in the Baltics confirming the benefits of local operational initiatives. [#62](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-62)

Despite the short-term headwinds, we remain confident in the region's fundamentals and continue to pursue selective growth opportunities especially where outsourcing potential remains underpenetrated. [#63](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-63)
Moving on to the next slide. [#64](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-64)

Let's now turn to the U.K. and Ireland, where continued productivity gains supported further margin improvement in the first half, bringing it close to 32%. [#66](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-66)

Reported revenue was up plus 4%, including plus 2.8% organic growth moderate but solid performance, especially considering the mixed market context. [#67](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-67)
Commercial momentum remained positive with many new contracts signed in hospitality. [#68](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-68)
However, activity levels among our clients were somewhat subdued in H1, which impacted volumes. [#69](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-69)
The pricing [indiscernible] was also softer than at year in line with the lower inflation observed in 2025 compared to 2024. [#70](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-70)
In addition, the region faced the calendar effect of approximately minus 0.3% on H1 growth. [#71](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-71)
On the positive side, we benefited from the appreciation of the British pound, which added plus 1.2% FX impact in the first half. [#73](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-73)
Despite these external factors, Elis continue to improve profitability in the region. [#74](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-74)

The EBITDA margin rose by 80 basis points to 31.9% thanks to effective cost control in workshop and logistics as well as ongoing productivity initiatives. [#75](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-75)
Let's now move on to Latin America, which delivered a solid organic growth in the first half despite temporary margin headwinds. [#76](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-76)
Momentum across the region remains strong with 7.3% organic growth. [#77](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-77)
Once again, confirming Latin America's role as a key growth engine. [#78](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-78)

In Brazil, organic growth was close to 10%, supported by strong performance in Healthcare, effective chair management and continued commercial success in workwear, including clean room services. [#79](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-79)
Mexico posted mid-single-digit organic growth. [#80](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-80)
Also some contract tenders were delayed towards the end of the year. [#81](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-81)
These tenders have since been secured and will start contributing to growth in the second half. [#82](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-82)

However, revenue was significantly impacted by currency depreciation, particularly in Brazil and Mexico, resulting in a minus 13.2% FX impact and a reported revenue decline of minus 5.9%. [#84](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-84)
On the profitability side, the EBITDA margin declined by 220 bps to 32.5%. [#85](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-85)

This was partly due to some one-off items, including recent government measures such as minimum wage increases, reduced working hours and the introduction of new labor premiums, many of which have not yet been fully reflected in our pricing. [#86](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-86)
In addition, operational performance in Brazil could have been stronger in the first half. [#87](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-87)

That said, we expect margin stabilization in the second half versus the second half of last year, supported by ongoing commercial renegotiations and continued productivity initiatives. [#88](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-88)

We now conclude our geographic review on Slide 13 with Southern Europe, which posted a strong commercial momentum and a stable margin in the first half. [#89](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-89)

Reported revenue increased by plus 9.5%, including plus 6.2% organic growth confirming our strong performance in Spain, Portugal and Italy. [#90](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-90)

Growth was driven by continued outsourcing momentum in workwear with new contract wins, including [indiscernible]  Good activity in hospitality, which remains a dominant segment in the region and solid performance in pest control supported by past bolt-on acquisition. [#91](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-91)
We also benefited from the integration of [indiscernible] in Spain, which added plus 3.2% to the regional growth in H1. [#92](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-92)
On the profitability side, the EBITDA margin came in at 31.8% virtually stable year-on-year, down just 10 bps. [#93](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-93)
This was due to an unfavorable calendar effect in the region. [#94](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-94)
Looking ahead, we expect the full year margin to improve, supported by continued volume growth and operational leverage. [#95](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-95)
Moving on to the next slide to conclude on M&A. [#96](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-96)
The group continued to execute its targeted bolt-on acquisition strategy. [#97](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-97)
with M&A contributing plus 1.8% to revenue growth in the first half. [#98](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-98)

Since the beginning of the year, 4 recently announced acquisitions have further strengthened our presence in key geographies and strategic market segments. [#100](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-100)
In Spain, we acquired Casa, a plant located near Madrid and focus on in hospitality clients. [#101](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-101)
The company generated around EUR 10 million in revenue in 2024. [#102](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-102)

Also in Spain [indiscernible] located south of Barcelona and dedicated to the hospitality market delivered approximately EUR 12 million in revenue last year. [#103](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-103)

In Germany, we acquired [indiscernible] which operates 2 plants serving [indiscernible] needs for health care and hospitality customers across Southern Germany and Northwest Austria. [#104](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-104)
One of the 2 sites is new and offer significant spare capacity, the company generated nearly EUR 20 million in 2024 revenue. [#105](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-105)

Finally, in Switzerland, we acquired Boden, which runs 2 plants covering Central and Eastern regions serving both hospitals and hotels. [#106](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-106)
The business generated EUR 27 million in 2024, and we anticipate significant logistics and industrial synergies. [#107](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-107)

These acquisitions are fully aligned with our bolt-on strategy, reinforcing local density, targeting high potential segments and creating long-term value through operational integration. [#108](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-108)
With that, I will now hand over to Deep who will provide more detail on our H1 2025 financial performance. [#110](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-110)
Thank you, Xavier. [#112](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-112)
Good afternoon, everyone. [#113](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-113)
Moving on to the next slide. [#114](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-114)
Let's first take a look at this chart, which we'd like to show regularly. [#115](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-115)
It illustrates the evolution of Elis revenue and EBITDA margin over more than 2 decades. [#116](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-116)
And it's fair to say that recent years have clearly confirmed the resilience and profitability of our business model. [#117](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-117)

This resilience relies on 2 main pillars: first, a well-diversified geography footprint with France now representing less than 1/3 of revenue; and second, a broad and balanced client base diversified both by sector and client size. [#118](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-118)

It's also worth highlighting that this profile has been further strengthened by our expansion into Latin America and the acquisition of [ Berendsen ], which structurally enhanced our growth potential and stability. [#119](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-119)

Looking at the graph, you can see that EBITDA margin has remained consistently high fluctuating within a narrow range even through major discrepancy like global financial crisis, COVID-19 recession, energy crisis following the war in Ukraine. [#121](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-121)
Remember that figures [indiscernible] include also the IFRS 16 impact. [#122](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-122)
Another key strength is our linen investments adjust automatically to top line trends. [#123](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-123)
As we saw in 2020, when revenue slows, investments dropped mechanically which preserves cash generation. [#124](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-124)
And that brings us to free cash flow. [#125](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-125)

Over the last 5 years, it has risen steadily from EUR 186 million in '19 to nearly EUR 350 million in '24 and we expect this upward trajectory to continue going forward. [#126](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-126)

Moving on to the next slide, let me walk you through the usual revenue breakdown by activity and the market and geography, which illustrates Elis highly diversified and well-balanced profile, whichever angle you look at activity, customer segment or geography you'll see that Elis is not dependent on any single category, which is a key strength, especially in times of micro, macro uncertainties. [#127](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-127)

By activity, revenue is split across flat linen, 46%, workwear 37% and [indiscernible] 17%, a mix that reflects the breadth of our service offering. [#128](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-128)
On the market side, we serve 4 major end markets: health care, 30%, industry 27%, hospitality, 25%; and health service, 18%. [#130](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-130)
Each segment is driven by different fundamentals and offers complementary growth drivers adding to our models overall stability. [#131](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-131)
And looking at geography, France represents only 30% of group revenue. [#132](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-132)

The rest shows a solid balance between mature regions like Central Europe, U.K., [indiscernible] and more dynamic regions as Latin America, Southern Europe, which offer strong growth potential. [#133](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-133)
This well-balanced decertification is no coincidence. [#134](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-134)
It is a result of a disciplined long-term strategy supported by marketing commercial execution and targeted M&A. [#135](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-135)
Moving on to next slide let's now take a look at revenue growth and the EBITDA margin by geography. [#137](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-137)

As Xavier mentioned, the total revenue growth of plus 4.3% includes 1.8% from M&A and minus 1% from ForEx, mainly due to the depreciation of currencies in Latin America. [#138](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-138)
All in all, organic growth was 3.5% or approximately when restated for the minus 50 bps of negative calendar effect in H1. [#139](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-139)

In a nutshell, top line is supported by commercial developments on the back of our 3 dimension strategy, product market size of clients, you see that particularly in Latin America and Southern Europe. [#140](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-140)

Second, hotels activity was good in France pay in Portugal, but low in U.K. And third, adverse calendar affected particularly [indiscernible] U.K.  For margin, that's another strong semester where no zones stand significantly below 32% in a nutshell, very good productivity performance everywhere. [#141](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-141)

Energy hedging impacting more or less the regions, some one-off underlined [indiscernible] calendar effect in Southern Europe and lag to pass staff inflation in Latin America. [#142](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-142)
Let's now take a look at the full P&L for the first half of '25. [#143](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-143)
So revenue reached EUR 2.34 billion, up 4.3% year-on-year. [#144](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-144)
Adjusted EBITDA increased by 5.1% to EUR 813.8 million with a margin of 34.7%, up 30 bps. [#145](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-145)
I will provide more details on this in the next slide. [#146](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-146)
But depreciation expenses represented 19.6% of revenue, up from 19.2% in '24. [#147](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-147)
This resulted in a slight 20 bps decline in EBIT margin to 15.1% of revenue, which stood at EUR 353.8 million, up 3% year-on-year. [#148](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-148)

Now below EBIT, the main items below EBIT and the operating income are noncurrent operating income and expense, which amounted to minus EUR 7.7 million, which is a standard amount for operational one-off like litigation or restructuring costs. [#150](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-150)
In '24, you remember that we had around EUR 32 million of earn-out revaluation in the EUR 14.8 million. [#151](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-151)

IFRS 2 expenses which corresponds to the accounting treatment of performance share plans rose to EUR 21.1 million compared to EUR 12.5 million last year. [#152](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-152)

This increase is linked to the 3-year rise in Elis share price impacting LTIP valuation, but also to the higher employer contribution rate in France, rising from 20% to 30% following recent government decisions and social policy as set out in the 2025 social [indiscernible]  And last, amortization of intangible assets from past acquisitions was stable at EUR 43.4 million as it is mostly linked to the 2017 acquisition of Berendsen and Labs.
